children: The Indian rupee slipped on Tuesday as oil prices advanced on risks the Middle East conflict will persist further after Iran threatened to retaliate against any new U.S. attacks.
Continued intervention from the Indian central bank limited the currency's fall.
fell past the psychologically important 94.50 level to 94.69 per dollar as of tktk IST, down 0.2% from the previous close.
State-run banks' dollar sales, most likely on behalf of the Reserve Bank of India, contained losses - as seen over recent trading sessions, traders said.

Brent crude climbed past $97 per barrel, hovering near its highest since late July after Iran threatened the U.S. with "economic warfare" and said it had fired an advanced missile at U.S. warships, highlighting the risk of a wider escalation.

Traders expect the strain to be managed by the RBI's persistent presence in the foreign exchange market. At the moment, the central bank is "managing a bulk of the dollar demand-supply mismatch," a trader at a private bank said.

As long as that pattern continues, the rupee is likely to hover in the 94.50 to 95 range with the balance of risks tilted towards rupee appreciation if the RBI elects to push it higher, the trader added.
Asian currencies were trading mixed and regional stocks were on the back foot. Stocks in Mumbai
fell 0.4%. Foreign investors have turned net sellers of Indian stocks and bonds in September, selling net $1.2 billion, reversing course after three months.

While the impact of anaemic portfolio flows over the last two years has been eroded by a range of policy measures that have drawn in a $137 billion haul, analysts say restoring "natural" capital flows will remain a key priority.

"India has been able to buy time for now, but over a longer horizon, the need to restore the efficacy of the capital account to finance a modest current account deficit India is likely to run is urgent," BofA Global Research said in a note.
